original_question: If G = lim-> Gn is the direct limit of an ascending sequence of finite-dimensional Lie groups with smooth inclusion homomorphisms, is G a topological group with Lie algebra in the sense of Hofmann and Morris? That is, do the continuous one-parameter subgroups Hom_c(R, G) carry the vector-space and Lie-bracket operations specified by Definition 3.1, with addition given by the Trotter-type limit of (gamma(t/n) eta(t/n))^n and bracket given by the commutator limit, so that Hom_c(R, G) becomes a topological Lie algebra naturally identified with L(G)?
target_in_paper: The paper’s third open problem, stated in the abstract/introduction and resolved in the main results: whether a direct limit Lie group G = varinjlim G_n of an ascending sequence of finite-dimensional Lie groups is a "topological group with Lie algebra" in the sense of Hofmann and Morris.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the relevant direct-limit setting G = varinjlim G_n, the Hofmann–Morris notion of a topological group with Lie algebra, the role of the continuous one-parameter subgroups Hom_c(R,G), the Trotter-type addition law, the commutator-limit bracket, and the intended identification with the Lie algebra L(G).
missing_details: It should say that G is the direct-limit Lie group attached to the ascending sequence, not merely the abstract direct limit as a group.
It should specify the topology on Hom_c(R,G), namely the compact-open topology used in the Hofmann–Morris setup.
It should include the full Hofmann–Morris operations, not only addition and bracket but also scalar multiplication (r·gamma)(t) = gamma(rt).
It should state the exact commutator formula, including the t^2 scaling in the standard bracket definition.
It should specify in what sense the Trotter and commutator limits are taken.
It should make explicit the canonical comparison map L(G) -> Hom_c(R,G), x |-> (t |-> exp_G(tx)).
It should clarify that the mathematical issue is not whether G is a topological group simpliciter, but whether its one-parameter subgroups carry the Hofmann–Morris topological Lie algebra structure.
It should keep the scope to the countable ascending sequence of finite-dimensional Lie groups considered in the paper, rather than a broader class of direct systems.
refined_question: Let G = varinjlim G_n be the direct-limit Lie group of an ascending sequence G_1 ⊆ G_2 ⊆ ··· of finite-dimensional real Lie groups with smooth inclusion homomorphisms. If Hom_c(R,G) denotes the space of continuous one-parameter subgroups of G, endowed with the compact-open topology and the Hofmann–Morris operations (gamma+eta)(t) := lim_{n->∞}(gamma(t/n)eta(t/n))^n, (r·gamma)(t) := gamma(rt), and [gamma,eta](t^2) := lim_{n->∞}(gamma(t/n)eta(t/n)gamma(-t/n)eta(-t/n))^{n^2}, does Hom_c(R,G) become a topological Lie algebra, and is the canonical map x |-> (t |-> exp_G(tx)) an isomorphism of topological Lie algebras L(G) ≅ Hom_c(R,G)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is every direct-limit Lie group G = varinjlim G_n arising from an ascending sequence of finite-dimensional Lie groups a topological group with Lie algebra in the sense of Hofmann and Morris?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper’s third problem rather than the neighboring Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2, which concern initial Lie subgroup structures. The abstract states the third problem almost verbatim, while the later discussion of the Hofmann–Morris definition supplies the precise meaning via Hom_c(R,G) and the Trotter/commutator limits. The refined version therefore keeps the paper’s exact scope and terminology, while adding the missing stand-alone data: the direct-limit Lie group structure on G, the compact-open topology on Hom_c(R,G), the full list of operations, the exact comparison map with L(G), and the fact that the real question is the Hofmann–Morris Lie algebra structure carried by one-parameter subgroups.
